key_insight: Semantic early-stopping replaces fixed iteration caps by halting LLM agent loops when meaning stops changing, reducing wasted tokens without hurting answer quality.
engineering_relevance: This enables more efficient multi-agent QA systems by shifting control from blind max-iterations to adaptive stopping policies that preserve quality on easy cases and save compute overall.
method: Track cosine distance between consecutive draft embeddings with a patience window.
Optionally gate stopping on a measured quality signal from an LLM judge.
Replay all stopping policies over the same generated trajectories with cached judge calls for fair comparison.
evidence_signal: On 60 HotpotQA test questions, the judge-free semantic stopper cut operational tokens by 38% versus max_iterations at parity quality, while the full quality-gated version was costlier due to judge overhead.
watch_item: Quality-gated stopping can be counter-productive in practice because per-round judge calls may dominate token cost, and the best-round oracle is not directly implementable.
paper_title: Semantic Early-Stopping for Iterative LLM Agent Loops
